battle.name: 郭威滅後漢之戰
battle.brief: 乾祐三年冬，樞密使郭威據鄴都河北兵柄，隱帝密詔加害，遂先發制人南下；大梁禁軍在劉子陂崩潰，帝出亡被弒，郭威入城廢劉贇，翌年改元廣順建後周。此役以譁變破城，非持久攻圍，投石機未及大用；然契丹圍內丘、太原倚砲石死守，攻城利器已見於戰局兩端。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方是三層：後漢中央、河北藩鎮與契丹騎軍。郭威自四月兼領鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使，樞密使如故，詔令河北兵甲錢穀「但見郭威文書立皆稟應」，河北的徵發與調度自此由一人握定，這是他在制度上取得的最大憑藉。中樞的指揮系統仍按五代舊制運作：樞密使楊邠總機政、郭威主征伐、侍衛親軍都指揮使史弘肇典宿衛、三司使王章掌財賦、宰相蘇逢吉同平章事，兵甲出內廷必經樞密院覆奏，蘇逢吉所謂「以內制外」正指此；禁軍分侍衛馬軍、步軍兩都指揮使，分屯京師與澶州，河北則有鄴都牙兵（馬軍都指揮使郭崇威、步軍都指揮使曹威）、天平軍節度使高行周、泰寧軍節度使慕容彥超、昭義軍節度使常思、忠武軍節度使楊信、安國軍節度使薛懷讓、成德軍節度使武行德等節鎮重兵，奉詔則發兵、詔止則還鎮。契丹方面由遼主耶律阮自將大軍南入河北，據鎮州、邢州奏報，騎兵以數萬計，並有後漢戍兵五百人叛應，開城迎敵，內丘、饒陽相繼失守。真正改寫對手的，是郭威從鄴都帶出的河北軍，以及大梁禁軍中整批倒向北軍的將士：二十日兩軍在劉子陂接戰，慕容彥超所部先挫，南軍多降，北軍遂能直抵城下。樞密院、禁軍、藩鎮三方在十日之內互相換位，是這場戰爭真正的結構。
countriesEn: Three layers took part in this war: the Later Han court at the eastern capital, the Hebei military circuits, and the Khitan horse. Since April Guo Wei had combined the offices of Yedu Circuit Commander and Tianxiong Army Commander while remaining Grand Marshal, and an edict ordered that all arms, pay and money in Hebei be answered on his own document alone; from that moment the raising and the movement of Hebei's resources rested in one pair of hands, which was the strongest legal warrant he obtained. The central command still worked on the old Five Dynasties pattern: Grand Marshal Yang Bin supervised the machinery of government, Guo Wei took charge of field operations, Guards Director Shi Hongzhao held the palace, Finance Commissioner Wang Zhang kept the treasury, and Chancellor Su Fengji sat as Vice Chancellor. Arms could not leave the inner court without the review of the Privy Council, which is exactly what Su Fengji meant by ruling the outer through the inner. The guards were divided between the cavalry and infantry command offices and garrisoned the capital and Chanzhou, while Hebei held the Yedu host under cavalry commander Guo Chongwei and infantry commander Cao Wei, together with the circuit armies of Gao Xingzhou of Tianping, Murong Yanchao of Taining, Chang Si of Zhaoyi, Yang Xin of Zhongwu, Xue Huairang of Anguo and Wu Xingde of Chengde; a circuit marched when the court ordered it and returned when the order was withdrawn. The Khitan side was the Liao ruler Yelü Ruan himself leading an army into Hebei; the reports from Zhenzhou and Xingzhou speak of tens of thousands of riders, and of five hundred Later Han garrison soldiers who defected and opened the gates, after which Neiqiu and Raoyang fell in turn. What actually reversed sides was the Hebei army Guo Wei brought down from Yedu and the body of capital guards who went over in whole companies to the northern army: on the twentieth day the two forces met at Liuzhi, Murong Yanchao's men were broken, and the southern troops deserted in droves, so that the northern host could come straight to the walls. In ten days the Privy Council, the guards and the circuits had exchanged places, and that is the true structure of this war.
people: 郭威（904年至954年），字文仲，邢州堯山人，早年為李克用部將李繼韜所賞識，後仕後漢，樞密使兼鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使，是本役的實際主導者；他的老臣樞密吏魏仁浦在密詔送到鄴都的當夜勸他「不可坐而待死」，他才留養子郭榮鎮鄴都、遣郭崇威將騎兵前驅、自將大軍南行。對面的漢隱帝劉承祐是劉知遠幼子，即位時年紀尚輕，性情暴烈，與李三娘（劉知遠之妻）及楊邠、史弘肇、王章等執政爭權，十一月十三日在東廡下殺楊邠、史弘肇、王章三人，並盡誅其親屬黨與；同日又遣供奉官孟業齎密詔赴澶州、鄴都，令鎮寧軍節度使李洪義殺王殷，令郭崇威與曹威殺郭威及王峻，正是這道密詔把局面推向兵變。內侍省使閻晉卿、飛龍使後匡贊、翰林茶酒使郭允明與武德使李業主謀滅執政，事後或自殺或奔亡。京師方面，劉銖在玄化門上射殺追兵左右，後被擒斬；侯益主張閉城固守以挫其鋒，慕容彥超自恃驍勇請出戰，兵敗奔兗州；竇貞固、蘇禹珪留守汴梁，李穀權判三司，馮道奉命赴宋州迎新君並以三十年舊相勸劉贇西行，范質則因詔書處分軍務合乎機宜而被郭威評為「宰相器」。河東的河東軍節度使劉崇與其子武寧軍節度使劉贇被挾以為帝，郭威廢贇為湘陰公，劉崇退守太原。契丹主耶律阮親率大軍入河北，旋因病歿於軍中，騎軍北還。
peopleEn: Guo Wei (904-954), courtesy name Wenzhong, was a native of Yaoshan in Xingzhou and the real author of this war. Early on he was noticed by Li Jintao, a general of Li Keyong, and later served the Later Han as Grand Marshal while holding Yedu Circuit Commander and Tianxiong Army Commander. His old clerk of the Privy Council, Wei Renpu, told him on the very night the secret edict reached Yedu that he could not sit and wait for death; only then did Guo Wei leave his adopted son Guo Rong to hold Yedu, send Guo Chongwei ahead with the cavalry and follow with the main army. On the other side stood the Later Han Emperor Yinzong, Liu Chengyou, the young son of Liu Zhiyuan. He was hot-tempered, fought with Empress Dowager Li and with the regents Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao and Wang Zhang, and on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month had the three regents killed in the eastern corridor of the palace, followed by the execution of their kinsmen and followers. The same day he sent the palace officer Meng Ye with secret edicts to Chanzhou and Yedu, ordering Li Hongyi to kill Wang Yin and Guo Chongwei and Cao Wei to kill Guo Wei and Wang Jun; that single edict pushed the situation into mutiny. The palace director Yan Jinqing, the flying dragon commissioner Hou Kuangzan, the literary and tea director Guo Yunming and the director of military works Li Ye had plotted the removal of the regents, and afterwards several of them killed themselves or fled. In the capital Liu Zhu stood on the Xuanhua gate and shot at the riders around the emperor; he was later taken and beheaded. Hou Yi argued for shutting the city and letting the attackers exhaust themselves, while Murong Yanchao, confident in his own valour, asked to give battle and fled to Yanzhou when beaten. Dou Zhenggu and Su Yugui stayed to hold Bianliang, Li Gu took charge of the Three Treasuries, Feng Dao was sent to Songzhou to fetch the new ruler and used his thirty years of service as an elder minister to persuade Liu Yun to go west, and Fan Zhi was judged by Guo Wei to have the makings of a chancellor because the court dispatches for military business always matched the situation. In Hedong, Liu Chong, the Hedong Army Commander, and his son Liu Yun, the Wuning Army Commander, were pushed forward as emperors; Guo Wei deposed Yun as Prince of Xiangyin, and Chong withdrew to Taiyuan. The Khitan ruler Yelü Ruan led his army into Hebei in person and died of illness in the field soon after, and the riders went north again.
kits: 卡面這具投石機（onager）在本役並非致勝之器，卻正是這場戰爭的隱喻：羅馬式的扭力拋臂與絞盤配重機制傳入中土之後，中原把它叫作「砲」、「砲車」、「飛石」或「拋石」，用途是攻守兩端的城頭高處。950年十一月契丹主將數萬騎入寇、攻內丘，五日不克而死傷其眾，靠的正是城上的飛石、檑木與突出的城樓；同樣的道理也在河東：郭威死後，晉王柴榮親征太原，先破迎春、孝義二寨，再拔北崗寨，築長壕圍城，造飛橋跨過城濠、穿地道逼城，而北漢守軍正以砲石為守城之柱，屢以飛石打壓攻城的將士。950年本身則是一場以奔襲與譁變破城的政變式戰爭，投石機沒有出手的機會，雙方主力是騎兵與步兵：郭威先以郭崇威的騎兵為前驅，禁軍劉子陂之役全靠馬隊衝鋒與夜襲；城防器械集中在偏廂拒馬、長竿、鹿角與弩，後漢禁軍的「飛石」多為手持或車載的小型拋射器，與卡面那具大型投石機分屬不同量級。弓弩方面，河北軍以步卒挽臂張弩與床子弩壓制騎兵，契丹騎兵則靠馬速與密集隊形衝撞；甲胄以札甲為主，缺甲的藩鎮兵與禁軍步卒相雜。攻城與守城的其餘要件同樣重要：壕塹、雲梯、飛橋、地道、隨軍攻城槓與轉輸用的車船糧秣，缺一不可。真正決定後漢命運的攻城技術並不是砲，而是騎兵與人心。
kitsEn: The onager on the card face never decided this war, yet it is a perfect emblem of it. The Roman machine, a torsion catapult arm worked by a winch and a counterweight, was known in China as the pao, the pao cart, the flying stone or the thrown stone, and its use was always the high ground of a wall, on either side of a siege. In the eleventh month of 950 the Khitan ruler brought tens of thousands of riders against Neiqiu, failed to take it in five days and lost many men doing so; what held the place was precisely the flying stones, the dropping beams and the projecting towers above the wall. The same logic reappeared in Hedong. After Guo Wei died the Prince of Jin, Chai Rong, campaigned on Taiyuan in person, broke the camps of Yingchun and Xiaoyi, took Beigang, built a long trench around the city, threw a flying bridge over the moat and drove a mine beneath the walls, while the Northern Han garrison made the pao-stone its pillar of defence, pounding the assaulting troops with stones again and again. The year 950 itself was a coup fought as a war, broken by a rush and a mutiny, and the onager had no chance to fire; the deciding arms on both sides were cavalry and infantry. Guo Wei led with the horse of Guo Chongwei, and the clash at Liuzhi was settled by the charge of mounted troops and by a night attack. The other defensive fittings were the side screens, the refuse forks, the long poles, the abatis and the crossbows; the flying stones of the Later Han guards were mostly small hand-thrown or cart-mounted projectors, a different order of magnitude from the big machine on the card. For bows, the Hebei infantry pressed the horsemen with drawn strong bows and bed crossbows, while the Khitan relied on the speed of the horse and on close order; armour was lamellar, and the under-armoured circuit troops fought mixed in with the guards. The rest of the siege and defence kit mattered just as much: the trench, the scaling ladder, the flying bridge, the mine, the assaulting beams carried with the army, and the carts, boats and grain that moved it all. What really decided the fate of the Later Han was not the pao, but cavalry and morale.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術可以分三段來看。第一段是「譁變式起兵」：密詔既到，郭威不逃不反，先留養子郭榮鎮鄴都以自保，再遣郭崇威將騎兵前驅，自己率大軍繼之，取「先發制人」之勢，由鄴都南下，旬日之間直抵大梁北面的封丘。第二段是大梁城下的攻心與夜襲：禁軍與北軍在劉子陂、赤岡、七里店一線列陣，慕容彥超恃勇以輕騎直衝，反而折了百餘人，士氣崩後南軍整批倒向北軍；隱帝宿於城外七里寨，京師禁軍盡潰，混戰中帝被亂兵弒於趙村民家；郭威本人並未攻城，而是以「誅群小」為名由迎春門入城，即命何福進部兵守明德門，禁止剽掠，至晚而定，把一場可能燒遍全城的洗劫壓成一夜之間受控的入城。第三段是對契丹的追擊與河北的收拾：十二月郭威自大梁發兵渡河，館於澶州，軍中數千人夜噪、裂黃旗披其身、呼萬歲震地，郭威順勢以「眾心所推」自居，南還而受監國，河北則分遣前驅取鎮州、定州，邊將奉「堅壁清野」之戒，無得擅出侵掠。若看城防的技術層面，同一套「守城靠砲石、攻城靠壕塹飛橋地道」的邏輯在河東重演：柴榮築壕圍太原、造飛橋渡城濠、穿地道進逼，守軍以飛石與弩砲反覆打壓，使攻方屢攻不克，最終仍靠攻城技術與內應取城。
tacticsEn: The campaign can be read in three movements. The first was a mutiny launched as an armed march. When the secret edict arrived, Guo Wei neither fled nor submitted; he left his adopted son Guo Rong at Yedu to hold the town, sent Guo Chongwei ahead with the cavalry and followed with the main army, taking the initiative before the order could be executed, and in a little over ten days he stood at Fengqiu north of Bianliang. The second was the breaking of the capital by rumour and by night. The guards and the northern army deployed along the line of Liuzhi, Chigang and Qilidian; Murong Yanchao, trusting his own courage, charged with light horse and lost more than a hundred men, and once that broke, whole companies of the southern army went over. The emperor spent the night at Qilidian outside the city, the capital guards dissolved, and in the confused fighting he was killed by stragglers in a farmhouse at Zhaocun. Guo Wei himself did not storm the walls. Entering by the Yingchun gate under the banner of punishing the evil ministers, he posted troops under He Fujin at the Mingde gate at once, forbade plunder, and by evening had the city quiet, compressing what might have been a city-wide conflagration into a controlled entry over one night. The third was the pursuit of the Khitans and the reordering of Hebei. In the twelfth month Guo Wei marched out of Bianliang, crossed the river and took up at Chanzhou; there several thousand of his own men clamoured at dawn, tore the yellow flag and wrapped it round him, and shouted for ten thousand years. Guo Wei accepted the position of a man raised by the army's will, turned south and received the regency, while in Hebei the advance troops were sent to take Zhenzhou and Dingzhou and the frontier officers were ordered to hold firm and not to raid on their own. At the level of technique the same logic repeated in Hedong: Chai Rong ringed Taiyuan with a trench, threw a flying bridge over the moat and drove his mine forward, while the defenders answered with flying stones and bolt-throwers, checked the assault again and again, and the city was finally taken by engineering combined with an opening from within.
data: 《資治通鑑》給這場戰爭留下的是一串可以核對的日期與幾組數字。乾祐三年即公元950年：四月壬午，郭威兼鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使，樞密使如故；十一月十三日（丙子）楊邠、史弘肇、王章被殺，同日密詔發往澶州、鄴都；十四日密詔到澶州，十五日郭威自鄴都發兵，二十日北軍抵封丘、兩軍遇於劉子陂，二十一日慕容彥超率輕騎先攻而折，二十二日隱帝出亡被弒於趙村民家，同日蘇逢吉、閻晉卿、郭允明自殺；二十四日郭威請李三娘早立嗣君，二十五日以劉贇承統；十二月十日澶州將士譁變、裂黃旗披郭威體，十日後郭威軍至七里店，十六日廢劉贇為湘陰公，十七日以侍中監國，翌年正月郭威即帝位，改元廣順。行程方面，郭威自鄴都至大梁不過旬日；奉迎新君的人事程序則「動涉浹旬」。契丹方面的規模是「將數萬騎入寇」，攻內丘五日不克，死傷其眾，並有戍兵五百人叛應契丹引其入城。太原之戰是另一組數字：柴榮自顯德元年入太原境外至顯德二年正月城破，前後圍城逾半年，先破迎春、孝義二寨，再拔北崗寨，漢主劉崇病死、劉希出降。投石機本身的規格沒有本役實測，只有通用工程估計：配重以噸計，石彈重數十斤，射程約一百五十至三百步，一具需數十人操作，每日可發射數十發，軍中須備直徑數尺的大木與粗繩。軍費一端，後漢因三叛連兵、宿兵累年仍能供給不匱，通鑑評王章聚斂刻急卻仍使「國家粗安」；郭威即位後清理田籍、整頓稅額，編戶增加三萬餘。
dataEn: The Zizhi Tongjian preserves for this war a series of dates that can be checked and a handful of figures. Qianyou year three was 950 AD. On the renwu day of the fourth month Guo Wei took Yedu Circuit Commander and Tianxiong Army Commander, remaining Grand Marshal as before. On the thirteenth day of the eleventh month, the bingzi day, Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao and Wang Zhang were killed, and the secret edicts went out to Chanzhou and Yedu the same day. On the fourteenth the edict reached Chanzhou; on the fifteenth Guo Wei marched out of Yedu; on the twentieth the northern army stood at Fengqiu and the two forces met at Liuzhi; on the twenty-first Murong Yanchao charged with light horse and was checked; on the twenty-second the emperor fled and was killed in a farmhouse at Zhaocun, and on the same day Su Fengji, Yan Jinqing and Guo Yunming killed themselves. On the twenty-fourth Guo Wei asked the empress dowager to appoint an heir early, and on the twenty-fifth the officers petitioned for Liu Yun to succeed. On the tenth day of the twelfth month the soldiers at Chanzhou clamoured, tore the yellow flag and wrapped it round Guo Wei; ten days later his army reached Qilidian; on the sixteenth Liu Yun was stripped of his title and made Prince of Xiangyin, and on the seventeenth Guo Wei was made regent. In the first month of the next year he took the throne and changed the era to Guangshun. In terms of movement, Guo Wei came from Yedu to Bianliang in no more than ten days, while the personnel business of fetching the new ruler took more than a full ten days. The Khitan force is described as tens of thousands of riders coming to raid; they failed against Neiqiu in five days and lost many men, and five hundred garrison soldiers defected and led them into the city. The siege of Taiyuan gives another set of figures: from the campaign of Xian De year one to the fall of the city in the first month of Xian De year two the investment lasted more than half a year, the camps of Yingchun and Xiaoyi fell first, then Beigang, the Han ruler Liu Chong died of illness and Liu Xi came out to surrender. There is no measurement of the onager taken in this war, only the usual engineering estimates: the counterweight is reckoned in tons, the stone weighs tens of jin, the range is about one hundred fifty to three hundred paces, one machine needs several dozen men to work and can fire dozens of times a day, and the army must carry timber of several chi in diameter together with heavy rope. On the fiscal side, the Later Han could still feed its armies after years of revolts and constant garrison duty, and the Tongjian says that though Wang Zhang was niggardly and severe, the state was still roughly at peace; after Guo Wei came to the throne he put the tax registers in order, and the number of registered households rose by more than thirty thousand.
cause: 後漢之亡不是一場外患造成的潰敗，而是幼主、女主、執政、宦官與藩鎮五方互相撕咬的結果。開國的高祖劉知遠死於乾祐元年，留下幼子劉承祐，並以李三娘攝行國政，政權由楊邠、史弘肇、王章、蘇逢吉等先帝舊臣分掌；隱帝年漸長而厭惡受制，與李業、聶文進、後匡贊、郭允明等內侍密謀，先殺楊邠、史弘肇、王章，再及黨與；而蘇逢吉、楊邠與史弘肇早已勢同水火，執政內鬥令軍中人人自危。外部壓力同樣真實：契丹主耶律阮自將大軍南入河北，趙州、鎮州一線城縣多陷，後漢戍兵甚至有五百人叛應契丹引其入城；京師為之戒嚴，澶州屯重兵，河北精兵與京師禁軍隔河相望。加上三司使王章刻薄聚斂，雀鼠耗改成「省耗」、錢陌由八十改為出七十七，鹽麴酒禁一經觸犯即以死罪繩之，軍將與士卒對朝廷的怨望無從宣洩。於是當密詔送到鄴都，殺郭威與王峻的指令攤開在桌上，這支軍隊立刻明白：郭威若死，河北諸軍奉詔而來，等於自己送死；郭威若生，事後朝廷追究屠京之罪，也未必有活路。譁變之所以在澶州爆發，正是這層計算的結果。
causeEn: The fall of the Later Han was not a collapse caused by foreign invasion; it was the result of five parties tearing at one another, the boy emperor, the empress dowager, the regents, the palace eunuchs and the circuits. The founder Liu Zhiyuan died in the first year of Qianyou, leaving a young son, Liu Chengyou, and the empress dowager Li, and the power was divided among the old ministers of the late emperor, Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Wang Zhang and Su Fengji. As the emperor grew he grew weary of being controlled, and with Li Ye, Nie Wenjin, Hou Kuangzan and Guo Yunming of the inner service he plotted and first killed Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao and Wang Zhang, then went on to their followers; meanwhile Su Fengji, Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao had already been at daggers, and the war of the regents left every soldier in the army anxious. The external pressure was just as real. The Khitan ruler Yelü Ruan led his army into Hebei in person, many towns on the Zhenzhou line fell, and five hundred Later Han soldiers defected and led the Khitans in through the gates. The capital was put on a footing of war, Chanzhou was heavily garrisoned, and the pick of the Hebei troops stood across the river from the capital guards. On top of this the finance commissioner Wang Zhang ground the people down, changing the old surtax of two sheng per hu into a 'reduction levy' of two dou, cutting the cash string from eighty to seventy-seven, and putting salt, yeast and liquor under penalties of death, so that the resentment of officers and men had nowhere to go. So when the secret edict reached Yedu and the order to kill Guo Wei and Wang Jun lay open, the army understood at once that if Guo Wei died, the Hebei forces would come in under an imperial order and bury themselves, while if he lived the court would afterwards pursue the crime of sacking the capital and they might not be left a living either. That calculation is why the mutiny broke at Chanzhou.
impact: 這場戰爭改變了中原的權力結構，也改變了兵器的用途史。後漢覆亡、郭威代漢建周，實際上是「禁軍—藩鎮」格局的重排：郭威以樞密使兼藩鎮的雙重身份執掌軍政，詔令河北只認郭威文書，這套做法後來被後周世宗柴榮推到極致——整肅禁軍、設殿前都點檢、罷藩鎮兵權，趙匡胤陳橋兵變時所繼承的，正是這支經過整頓的中央禁軍。制度面上，郭威清算後漢苛政，減免賦稅、破宮中珍玩以示節儉、清理田籍，編戶增加三萬餘，恢復了戰亂以來被摧殘的田賦基礎；臨終又托付喪事從簡，不得叨擾百姓。北方局勢方面，契丹因主帥病歿而退回，塞北南下的通道暫時關閉，中原獲得喘息的空間；對後世而言，這場政變打斷了劉氏「漢」的正統，把河東另立的北漢壓成偏安一隅的殘政，四年後柴榮破太原，漢祚至此才真正斷絕，而後周三征南唐、統一江南，也就此為北宋一統的南北格局鋪平了道路。兵器史上的位置更為直接：自羅馬拋石機之後，中原的「砲」在唐宋兩代從守城利器逐漸變成攻城主力，柴榮太原之役、趙匡胤采石之役都有拋石機的身影，攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力，也從此有了可以計算的開支與風險。
impactEn: This war rearranged the balance of power in the central plains and also changed the working life of the weapon on the card. The fall of the Later Han and Guo Wei's substitution of the Zhou for the Han was in truth a reordering of the guards-and-circuits pattern: holding the Grand Mastership and a great circuit at the same time, Guo Wei governed army and state together, and the rule that Hebei answered only on his own document was later pushed to its extreme by the Zhou Emperor Shizong, Chai Rong, who disciplined the guards, created the office of commander of the palace forces and took the troops of the circuits back into the centre. The central force that Zhao Kuangyin inherited when he seized the throne at Chenqiao was precisely that disciplined central army. In institutional terms Guo Wei swept away the harsh regulations of the Later Han, remitted taxes, smashed the palace treasures to show austerity, put the tax registers in order, and raised the number of registered households by more than thirty thousand, restoring a tax base that the wars had ruined; on his deathbed he ordered his own funeral to be plain and bade that the people be not troubled. In the north, the Khitans withdrew after their commander died, the road from the steppe into the heartland was shut for a time, and the central plains gained room to breathe. For posterity the coup cut the legitimate line of the Liu house's Han, pressed the Northern Han raised in Hedong into a remnant state in one corner, and four years later, when Chai Rong took Taiyuan, the Han was ended in truth; the three campaigns against Southern Tang that followed, and the unification of the south, paved the way for the north-south order of the Northern Song. The place of the weapon in history is just as direct: since the Roman throwing engine, the pao of the Chinese had moved from a defensive instrument to the main arm of assault, appearing in Chai Rong's siege of Taiyuan and in Zhao Kuangyin's fight at Caishi, and from that point a siege had a destructiveness that could be calculated - and a cost and a risk that could be calculated as well.
result: 結果是後漢政權在乾祐三年十一月十九日之後連根拔除。二十二日隱帝出亡被弒，蘇逢吉、閻晉卿、郭允明自盡，劉銖、李洪建被擒斬於市，郭威入大梁後封明德門、禁兵勿掠，二十四日請李三娘臨朝聽政並議立嗣君；起初眾將請立高祖之子劉承勛，因久羸疾不獲用，轉而迎高祖之弟、河東軍節度使劉崇之子武寧軍節度使劉贇，十二月十六日廢贇為湘陰公、幽閉京師，十七日以侍中監國，翌年正月郭威即真人之位，改元廣順；後漢兩陵因國亡而不得一祭。契丹騎軍在內丘、饒陽受挫，又折主帥，北還而去，河北重歸朝廷版籍；郭威留鎮中原，整軍經武，削平兗州李崧之亂，先後封養子柴榮為晉王，954年正月朔改元顯德，同月十六日郭威病崩，年五十，留下由柴榮收拾的殘局。柴榮隨即親征河東，955年正月攻破太原，北漢主劉崇病死、劉希開城出降，漢祚至此而絕，這場起於950年冬的戰爭才算走完最後一步。
resultEn: The outcome was that the Later Han state was torn out by the roots after the nineteenth day of the eleventh month of Qianyou year three. On the twenty-second the emperor fled and was killed; Su Fengji, Yan Jinqing and Guo Yunming killed themselves; Liu Zhu and Li Hongjian were taken and beheaded in the market; and once Guo Wei was inside Bianliang he sealed the Mingde gate and forbade the troops to plunder. On the twenty-fourth he asked the empress dowager Li to take the regency in person and the question of an heir was put to the assembly. The officers first proposed Liu Chengxu, a son of the founder, but he had been weakly for so long that he could not be brought forward, and they turned instead to Liu Yun, the Wuning Army Commander, who was a son of Liu Chong, the late emperor's younger brother and the Hedong Army Commander. On the sixteenth day of the twelfth month Yun was demoted to Prince of Xiangyin and shut up in the capital, and on the seventeenth Guo Wei took the regency; in the first month of the next year he took the throne and changed the era to Guangshun, and the two mausoleums of the Han house were never once sacrificed to before the state was gone. The Khitan riders were checked at Neiqiu and Raoyang, lost their commander, went north, and Hebei returned to the registers of the court. Guo Wei held the central plains, put the army in order, put down the revolt of Li Song at Yanzhou, made his adopted son Chai Rong Prince of Jin, changed the era to Xiande on the first day of the first month of 954, and died of illness on the sixteenth of that same month at the age of fifty, leaving the mess to Chai Rong. Chai Rong campaigned into Hedong at once, took Taiyuan in the first month of 955, the Northern Han ruler Liu Chong died of illness and Liu Xi opened the gate and surrendered, and the Han was ended for good. Only then was the last step of the war begun in the winter of 950 walked to the end.
